why: Both involve non-canvas or canvas-adjacent jokes in the room, and distinguishing ordinary sub talk from in-jokes played in canvas talk is the hardest line in this batch.

why.T3-011: Concepts show the room's members sending pixels or effort to help other rooms' works (r/furry Snoo, YiffMeDaddy, another maker's artwork), which is T3-011's gate.
why.T3-122: Several concepts are thanks/compliments addressed to other rooms (outsider, Touhou neighbour, Mass Effect maker) with no deal attached, matching T3-122's gate.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-011 covers helping other rooms' works but does not reach the acts of thanking/greeting other rooms for help, which are a distinct part of this item.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0481477, C0431278, C0481996, and C0173269 are thanks/compliments sent to other rooms with no deal attached, satisfying T3-122.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-122, because the item's main thrust is giving help; dropping it loses the thanks/greeting aspect but leaves the core placement.

why.T3-017: The YIFF mixtape exchange is ordinary sub talk and a bounded in-joke distinct from canvas work and the real-animal April Fools turn, matching T3-017's gate.

why.T3-005: Calls to reclaim what is ours and naming a Touhou hijack frame canvas changes as an attack to fight back against, satisfying T3-005's defence gate.

why.T3-023: The moderators announce a brand-new direction and change the sub's subject to real animals for April Fools, a whole-sub takeover played inside by members.

why.T3-017: The final fishman/birdman flair count and closing of new picks is a pre-existing room contest, i.e. ordinary sub business rather than canvas work.

why.T3-088: Reporting a phone glitch that gives unlimited pixels is placing beyond the one-pixel limit, satisfying T3-088.

why.T3-017: Recruiting a new moderator through a public search and Google form is ordinary sub maintenance, not canvas planning or rule change.

why.T3-185: Moderators clarify and members dispute posting rules (sexual content, low effort, repeated posts), and rules are adjusted, matching T3-185's gate for changing the sub's posting rules.

why.T3-005: Calls to defend Snoo and the sign, reports of constant attacks and attempts to turn the F into a swastika, and pledges to guard it all satisfy T3-005's defence-against-attackers gate.

why.T3-097: The moderators explicitly end the real-animal April Fools rules and switch back to old rules, which is T3-097's switching-off gate.
why.T3-100: They also give April Fools posts a participation flair so they are not deleted, keeping an April Fools change after the day, matching T3-100.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-097 covers switching off the April Fools rule change but does not reach the decision to keep participating posts via a participation flair after the day.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1481743 gives April Fools posts a participation flair so they will not be deleted, satisfying T3-100's gate of keeping an April Fools change.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-100, because the item's main action is the switch back; dropping it loses the commemoration aspect.

why.T3-023: Members recognize and play along with the moderators' real-animal April Fools takeover, extending the joke and mock-policing it, which is playing inside the sub's changed state.

why.T3-088: Reporting a phone glitch that gives unlimited pixels is placing beyond the one-pixel limit, satisfying T3-088.

why.T3-031: Members notice the corrupted canvas lettering and play out new names (furby, forry, furay) as a running joke, which is playing the room's in-jokes in canvas talk.

why.T3-063: The passages assess a canvas progress post as late and ask whether to take it down, which is handling a canvas post under the sub's rules and contesting a removal.
